claims.text: The rider did not simply go silent. Inside the waiting window she sent the locating message 'coming down now' at 22:14:42, which the record shows the driver read at 22:15:12, and the driver neither replied in the chat within 120 seconds of that message nor placed any in-app voice call — trip_record.in_app_calls is empty — before cancelling at 22:19:14. That unanswered-coordination pattern is exactly what POL-NS-04(a) and (b) are written to capture, and it weighs for the rider rather than against her.

The record does not affirmatively place the rider at the pickup. derived.arrival.rider_qualifying_fix_count is 0 against the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius, so POL-NS-04(c) — which needs the rider inside 100 m for the majority of qualifying fixes — cannot be run to find her away from the pin, and under POL-NS-11 an unrunnable presence limb is UNDECIDABLE, not failed. The judge must say the test could not be run and may not draw an adverse inference against the rider from it.

The chat log and the rider's own track cannot both be describing the same moment: the chat has the rider typing 'coming down now' at 22:14:42 while the rider_track reports a stationary device roughly 713 m from the pin (derived.rider_presence.mean_distance_m, min 709.8 m, max 717.2 m). No clause on this record resolves that conflict on rider presence, so the case should go to human review under POL-NS-09 and the $4.50 held rather than collected while the reviewer settles it.

The arrival here rests on a driver-pressed BUTTON marker (trip_record.platform_policy.arrival_marker = BUTTON), and POL-NS-12's platform-confirmation shortcut is expressly limited to GPS_AUTO arrivals. The driver therefore takes no presumption from the tap: the fee can stand only if he discharges POL-NS-02's own test — at least three consecutive in-radius fixes inside the 50 m STANDARD radius at 25 m accuracy or better — and POL-NS-01(c)'s continuously measured dwell. The rider does not concede those limbs.

claims.text: The trip record carries every driver-side fact POL-NS-01 requires: a driver 'arrived' event at 22:12:22, no boarding event anywhere in the record, and a termination by the driver at 22:19:14 under cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW. All four limbs of the baseline chargeable no-show anchor clause are therefore live on this record.

The driver's GPS trace places him inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius in a single continuous qualifying run of 410 seconds, from 22:12:22 to 22:19:12 - more than double the 180-second free waiting period in force for this trip under POL-NS-01(c), and the run begins at the exact timestamp of the 'arrived' event.

POL-NS-02's proximity test is satisfied independently of the marker: the trace contains 42 qualifying in-radius fixes, far more than the three consecutive accuracy-filtered fixes the clause requires, so absence or sparsity of evidence is not in play.

The arrival marker is not FALSE under POL-NS-05. The driver's first qualifying in-geofence fix is at 22:12:22, the same instant as the 'arrived' event, so at the marker the driver was inside the arrival radius and stationary - not more than 300 m from the pin and not travelling at 15 km/h or more. No false-arrival recomputation of the waiting clock is triggered and the 410-second dwell stands as measured from 22:12:22.

POL-NS-03 is not the governing clause and supplies the rider no relief: the driver's stationary fixes lie INSIDE the POL-NS-02 radius, not outside it but within 400 m, so this is not a wrong-entrance or wrong-block case and the fee is not refunded under it.

There is no waiting-period shortfall under POL-NS-06. Measured against the 180-second minimum the dwell of 410 seconds leaves a shortfall of -230 seconds; the cancellation came at 22:19:14, after the required dwell had elapsed, so no refund is licensed by this clause.

The rider's own device track defeats his 'I was only a few minutes late' account and defeats any POL-NS-04 exoneration. Even assuming the rider's 22:14:42 message counts as locating or coordinating (limb (a)) and that the driver did not reply within 120 seconds (limb (b)), limb (c) is affirmatively failed on admissible fixes: every rider fix sits roughly 710 m from the pickup pin - far outside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius - and the count of qualifying rider fixes is zero. POL-NS-04 therefore does not apply and the dispute is decided under POL-NS-01.

The chat log corroborates a genuine wait by a present driver: he announced his arrival at 22:12:47 ('hi im at the pickup point, where are you'), the rider's only reply came at 22:14:42, and the driver nevertheless held position until 22:19:14, cancelling well over two full free waiting periods after arriving.

No traffic advisory covers this pickup - EV-ADVIS-03301-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0, which I disclose - but nothing turns on it. The dwell is a single unbroken in-geofence run, so POL-NS-06 limb (i) accumulation across separate intervals is not needed and the absent advisory neither helps nor hurts the driver here.

Compensation is payable under POL-NS-07: 80 percent of the SGD 4.50 fee in force is SGD 3.60, and the anti-farming check does not trip - no_show_terminations_30d is 1, below the threshold of 4, and 1 divided by completed_trips_30d of 86 is about 0.012, far below the 0.08 rate. Compensation is therefore paid, not withheld.

The fare breakdown shows the SGD 4.50 no-show fee charged with payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd at 0.00, consistent with a verified no-show. On this rider-filed dispute the outcome the record produces is DRIVER_COMPENSATION with amount_sgd mirroring the SGD 3.60 driver payment fixed by POL-NS-07 - the fee stands and the driver is owed money, and NO_ACTION would be a misreading of POL-GEN-03.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver: the $4.50 no-show fee charged on TRP-03301 stands, and the driver is to be paid SGD 3.60.

Why the charge stands. POL-NS-01 requires four things and all four are on this record. (a) EV-TRIP-03301 carries the driver's 'arrived' event at 22:12:22. (b) EV-GPS-03301 places the driver inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius from 22:12:22 - 42 accuracy-filtered in-radius fixes, far more than the three consecutive fixes POL-NS-02 requires, the first of them at the same instant as the marker. (c) The driver held position continuously for 410 seconds (22:12:22 to 22:19:12) against the 180-second free waiting period in force for this trip (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec = 180; no_show_threshold_sec is null). (d) There is no boarding event, and the driver terminated the trip at 22:19:14 under RIDER_NO_SHOW, after the required dwell had elapsed at 22:15:22.

The arrival marker is not false. Under POL-NS-05 the test is the driver's position and speed at the marker: at 22:12:22 he was inside the radius and stationary, not more than 300 m away and not at 15 km/h or more, so the waiting clock is not recomputed. POL-NS-03 does not apply - his stationary fixes are inside the radius, not outside it but within 400 m. POL-NS-06 gives no relief: the 410-second dwell exceeds the 180-second minimum by 230 seconds, so there is no shortfall to refund, and the absent advisory is not needed because accumulation across separate intervals is not required for a single unbroken run.

The rider's arguments. I accept that the rider sent a message during the waiting window ('coming down now', 22:14:42) and that the driver neither replied within 120 seconds (though he read it at 22:15:12) nor placed an in-app call. But POL-NS-04 needs all three limbs, and limb (c) fails: the rider's own device track sits roughly 710-717 m from the pickup pin across all 62 fixes, far outside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius, so the rider is not exonerated. POL-NS-11 does not rescue that finding - it applies where the rider track is absent or wholly filtered out, and here the track is present and admissible; limb (c) is failed, not undecidable. I also decline the request to escalate under POL-NS-09: the chat and the track do not contradict each other directly on rider presence - 'coming down now' is a statement of intention, and POL-NS-04(c) is the clause that resolves rider presence. The rider is right that the BUTTON arrival marker earns no POL-NS-12 platform-confirmation presumption, but the driver establishes POL-NS-02 on his own evidence regardless.

Driver compensation. The fee in force is SGD 4.50 (EV-FARE-03301, matching trip_record.platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd). Under POL-NS-07 the driver is paid 80 percent = SGD 3.60. The anti-farming check does not trip: no_show_terminations_30d is 1 (below 4) and 1 divided by 86 completed trips is about 0.012 (below 0.08), so compensation is paid rather than withheld.

Because the driver is owed money, the ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION and amount_sgd carries the same SGD 3.60 figure under POL-GEN-03; the rider's $4.50 charge stands as it presently is. The missing traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-03301-01 (weight 0.0) carries no fact here, as nothing relied on it. The monetary effect, SGD 3.60, is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, so it executes automatically on issue (POL-GEN-05).

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: this was a verified no-show and the SGD 4.50 cancellation fee stands.

Rider — your account that you were only a few minutes late is not supported by the record. The driver tapped 'I'm Here' at 22:12:22 and the GPS trace independently places him inside the 50 m pickup geofence from 22:12:22 to 22:19:12, one continuous run of 410 seconds with 42 accuracy-qualified in-radius fixes. That satisfies POL-NS-02 (the required 3 consecutive in-radius fixes) and the continuous-dwell test of POL-NS-01(c), at more than twice the 180-second free waiting period in force for this trip. No boarding event was recorded and the trip was terminated by the driver at 22:19:14 under reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW, so all four limbs of POL-NS-01 hold. Your own device track sits about 710 m from the pickup pin throughout the window (rider_qualifying_fix_count 0 against the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius), so POL-NS-04 (rider contact unanswered) cannot exonerate you: its limb (c) is not met on your own track, and under POL-NS-11 even an unrunnable presence limb would not help you. Your 22:14:42 message 'coming down now' was delivered and read at 22:15:12, but the driver had already served the waiting period he was entitled to. Your request to escalate under POL-NS-09 is declined: the claimed conflict between your chat message and your device track concerns rider presence, not the driver's arrival or dwell, which no artifact contradicts, and POL-NS-04/POL-NS-11 already answer rider presence, so there is no unresolved conflict on a deciding fact.

Driver — your marker is not a false arrival. The first qualifying in-geofence fix is at 22:12:22, the same instant as the 'I'm Here' tap, so POL-NS-05 does not recompute the waiting clock and no false-arrival referral arises. Because POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it, you are compensated under POL-NS-07 at 80% of the SGD 4.50 fee in force = SGD 3.60. The anti-farming check does not trip (no_show_terminations_30d = 1, below 4; 1 divided by 86 completed trips is about 0.01, below 0.08), so compensation is paid rather than withheld. The advisory EV-ADVIS-03301-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0) but nothing turns on it: the dwell is a single unbroken in-geofence run and POL-NS-06(i) accumulation is not needed, so its absence neither helps nor hurts.

Result: DRIVER_COMPENSATION. Per POL-GEN-03, amount_sgd mirrors the SGD 3.60 driver payment — that is the amount the ruling moves; the rider's SGD 4.50 charge stands. No referral is produced: the marker is not false and RIDER_NO_SHOW is a correct reason code. Confidence 0.9, capped at 1.0 because every artifact carrying a deciding fact carries weight 1.0. The monetary effect (SGD 3.60) is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold and may execute automatically.

ruling.explanation:
This ruling concerns the SGD 4.50 no-show cancellation fee charged on trip TRP-03301 (EV-FARE-03301, total_charged 4.50, payment_status CHARGED). The outcome is a payment to the driver, not a refund to the rider.

Why the fee stands. The record satisfies every limb of POL-NS-01. (a) The trip record (EV-TRIP-03301) carries a driver 'arrived' event at 22:12:22. (b) The GPS trace (EV-GPS-03301) places the driver inside the 50 m STANDARD pickup radius at exactly that instant — his first qualifying in-geofence fix is at 22:12:22 with dwell_start_offset_sec 0.0 — so no POL-NS-05 recomputation of the clock is triggered. (c) He then held position continuously for 410 seconds, to 22:19:12, against the free waiting period of 180 seconds in force (EV-TRIP-03301.platform_policy.free_wait_sec): 42 accuracy-filtered in-radius fixes in one unbroken run. (d) The record shows no boarding event and a driver termination at 22:19:14 under cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, well after the 180-second dwell elapsed.

Driver's points. I accept the POL-NS-02, POL-NS-03, POL-NS-05 and POL-NS-06 arguments. POL-NS-02's own test is independently satisfied by 42 qualifying in-radius fixes, far beyond the three consecutive 25 m-accurate fixes the clause requires, so arrival does not depend on the marker. POL-NS-05 does not fire: at 22:12:22 the driver was inside the radius and stationary, neither more than 300 m from the pin nor moving at 15 km/h. POL-NS-06 is not engaged: the 410-second dwell exceeds the 180-second minimum, leaving no shortfall (-230 s). POL-NS-03 does not govern: the stationary fixes lie inside the POL-NS-02 radius, not outside it but within 400 m. The chat log (EV-CHAT-03301) is consistent with a present driver — he announced his arrival at 22:12:47 and remained until 22:19:14.

Rider's points. Your POL-NS-04 exoneration argument fails. Even taking your 22:14:42 message as locating or coordinating (limb (a)) and the driver's non-reply within 120 seconds with no in-app call (limb (b)), limb (c) is not met: your own device track (EV-GPS-03301) records your device stationary roughly 710 m from the pin throughout, with no fix inside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius (rider_qualifying_fix_count is 0), so the rider was not at the pickup. If the track were instead treated as unrunnable, POL-NS-11 makes limb (c) undecidable rather than failed, and the clause still cannot exonerate you — the fee is decided on the driver's own evidence. Either way POL-NS-04 does not apply. Your POL-NS-09 escalation argument also fails: the supposed conflict between your 'coming down now' message and your device's position goes to whether the rider was at the pickup, which is not the fact that decides this fee — the driver's arrival and dwell are, and those are consistent across the trip record and the trace. POL-NS-04(c), read with POL-NS-11, is the clause that governs rider presence, so POL-NS-09(b)'s 'no clause resolves the conflict' condition is not satisfied, and no other POL-NS-09 trigger (confidence, repeat-party disputes, anti-farming, sole impaired evidence) is present. You are right that arrival rests on a driver-pressed BUTTON marker, so POL-NS-12's platform-confirmation shortcut does not apply; I give the marker no presumption — and none is needed, because POL-NS-02's own test is met.

The money. Because POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it, POL-NS-07 fixes the driver's payout at 80 percent of the SGD 4.50 fee in force = SGD 3.60 (the net figure, not the SGD 6.61 gross). The anti-farming check does not trip: no_show_terminations_30d is 1 (below 4) and 1/86 ≈ 0.012 (below 0.08), so compensation is paid rather than withheld. Under POL-GEN-03 this is a DRIVER_COMPENSATION ruling, in which amount_sgd carries the same SGD 3.60 the ruling moves and the rider's SGD 4.50 charge stands. No clause produces a referral. Confidence is 0.9: the deciding facts are carried by EV-TRIP-03301 and EV-GPS-03301, both at weight 1.0, so nothing caps confidence below that, and the SGD 3.60 monetary effect is within the SGD 8.00 automatic-execution threshold (POL-GEN-05).

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: this is decided on the recorded facts, not on how many minutes anyone believes they were late.

What happened and what was charged. The driver tapped 'I'm Here' at 22:12:22 and cancelled at 22:19:14 under reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW. The $4.50 cancellation fee (platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd = 4.50) was charged to the rider's card; the fare ledger shows it outstanding (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00, total_charged 4.50).

The baseline test (POL-NS-01) holds on all four limbs.
(a) The trip record carries the driver's 'arrived' event at 22:12:22.
(b) The GPS trace places him inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius at that same moment. POL-NS-12 does not apply because the marker is a driver-pressed BUTTON, not GPS_AUTO — the rider is right about that — but the driver then has to meet POL-NS-02 directly, and he does: the trace contains 42 qualifying in-radius fixes against the 3 consecutive accuracy-filtered fixes the clause requires.
(c) The driver held position inside the geofence for a single continuous 410 seconds (22:12:22 to 22:19:12), against the free waiting period of 180 seconds in force for this trip (platform_policy.free_wait_sec = 180; no_show_threshold_sec is not set).
(d) No boarding event is recorded, and the driver terminated the trip under RIDER_NO_SHOW at 22:19:14, after the required dwell had elapsed.
The arrival marker is not FALSE under POL-NS-05: at 22:12:22 the driver was at the pin and stationary — not more than 300 m away and not travelling at 15 km/h or more — so no waiting clock is recomputed. POL-NS-06 shows no shortfall (410 s against a 180 s minimum; the derived shortfall_sec of −230 s is a surplus). POL-NS-03 does not apply: the driver's stationary fixes lie inside the arrival radius, not outside it within 400 m.

The rider's arguments, answered.
POL-NS-04 (unanswered coordination): you did send a message at 22:14:42 ('coming down now') and the driver neither replied within 120 seconds nor placed an in-app call. But POL-NS-04 also requires your device to be within 100 m of the pin for the majority of your qualifying fixes. Your own track places your device about 713 m from the pin (mean 713.6 m; range 709.8–717.2 m) across all 62 fixes, so limb (c) fails on admissible fixes and the clause does not exonerate you.
POL-NS-11 (undecidable presence): it does not apply. POL-NS-11 covers a rider_track that is absent or wholly filtered for accuracy. Your track is present and unfiltered, so limb (c) is failed, not undecidable.
POL-NS-09 (escalation): I do not find a direct, unresolved contradiction. POL-NS-04(c) is the clause that decides rider presence and it resolves the point against your account, and the fee itself is carried by the driver-side records at full weight. None of the escalation triggers fires.

Driver's position. The fee stands.
